text: A European education fair opened in Budapest this week, drawing thousands of international applicants interested in Hungarian universities, scholarships, and residence procedures. Organizers said booths covered public universities and state scholarship programmes. Visitors asked about application deadlines, language requirements, and permit timelines. Officials urged students to read government factsheets before filing online cases. The event closes on Sunday.
summary: Budapest hosted a large education fair for international students. University and scholarship booths answered questions on deadlines and permits. Officials told visitors to check government factsheets before applying.

text: Hungary’s immigration authority updated a public factsheet describing how students extend residence permits for studies. The page stresses online filing through Enter Hungary and lists documents that must be uploaded. Applicants are reminded to appear for biometrics after submission. Universities often help students gather enrolment certificates. The authority said paper counters remain limited.
summary: Hungary updated student permit-extension guidance. Filing is online via Enter Hungary with required uploads. Biometrics follow submission, and universities may help with certificates.

text: Tempus Public Foundation published reminders about Stipendium Hungaricum living allowances for the coming academic year. The note distinguishes bachelor, master, and doctoral monthly amounts. Payments are made by host institutions while student status remains active. Scholars were told to track dormitory versus accommodation allowance rules. Old regulation PDFs should not be used when newer operational rules apply.
summary: Tempus reminded scholars about Stipendium living allowances. Amounts differ by study level and are paid by hosts. Students should follow current operational rules, not outdated PDFs.

text: ELTE released an international student guide covering programme lengths and credit expectations. Bachelor, master, one-tier, and doctoral paths are summarised in English. The guide points readers to faculty pages for course details. Advisers said the document complements, but does not replace, academic regulations. New arrivals were encouraged to download the latest PDF.
summary: ELTE’s international guide outlines programme lengths and credits. It supplements faculty pages and academic regulations. New students should use the latest PDF.

text: BME confirmed that when English and Hungarian study-code texts disagree, the Hungarian version prevails. The English Code of Studies remains an official translation for international students. Faculty offices continue to answer timetable and examination questions. Student unions circulated the clarification before the semester start. Administrators asked students to cite the current PDF.
summary: BME restated that Hungarian study-code text prevails on conflicts. The English translation still helps international students. Offices told students to cite the current PDF.

text: An EU portal page for students in Hungary reiterated extension conditions, including holding a valid permit when applying and meeting prior residence-day requirements. The portal links national procedures and Enter Hungary. Mobility under Directive 2016/801 is mentioned for short stays linked to another member-state permit. Advisers warned that national forms still control filing. Students should compare portal text with OIF factsheets.
summary: The EU student portal repeated Hungary extension conditions. It references Enter Hungary and Directive 2016/801 mobility. National OIF factsheets remain essential for filing.

text: John von Neumann University refreshed its English regulations index for international students. The page links academic regulations, study guides, and visa-related university notices. Staff said PDF links are updated when senate rules change. Applicants were advised not to rely on screenshots shared in chats. The university mailbox remains open for document questions.
summary: NJE updated its English regulations index with academic and visa links. Students should open current PDFs, not chat screenshots. The university mailbox handles document questions.

text: A doctoral Stipendium call for the next intake separates PhD rules from bachelor and master instructions. Research-plan requirements and host statements differ from taught-programme calls. Application accounts must upload the doctoral document list. National nominating partners still pre-screen in some countries. Incomplete research plans are a common rejection reason.
summary: The doctoral Stipendium call is separate from BA/MA rules. Research plans and host statements are required. Incomplete plans often cause rejection.

text: Government decree text on the national legislation site requires an academic-progress certificate from the educational institution when students extend study residence permits. Universities issue the certificate after checking enrolment and progress. Immigration cases filed without it can stall. Student advisers prepared template request emails. The decree is published in Hungarian.
summary: A government decree requires an academic-progress certificate for permit extensions. Universities issue it after progress checks. Missing certificates can stall immigration cases.

text: Employers hiring third-country student workers in Hungary were reminded of notification duties toward the aliens-policing authority. Host organizations share related obligations in some internship settings. Factsheets list timing expectations for notifications. HR teams were told to keep copies of residence documents. Failure to notify can trigger fines under national rules.
summary: Employers of third-country student workers face notification duties. Host organizations may share obligations for internships. Missing notices can lead to fines.

text: Enter Hungary’s student upload manual shows screenshot steps for creating a study-permit case online. Scholarship holders may see fee exemptions listed for certain Hungarian State Scholarships. Photo rules include format and size limits. Users must save the case number after submission. Support pages warn against sharing passwords.
summary: The Enter Hungary student manual covers online case steps and photo rules. Some scholarship holders have listed fee exemptions. Applicants should save case numbers and never share passwords.

text: Directive 2016/801 remains the EU framework for third-country students, researchers, and related categories. Member states implement procedures through national law. Short-term mobility certificates appear for some students already admitted elsewhere in the EU. Universities brief exchange offices each semester. Authentic text is on EUR-Lex.
summary: Directive 2016/801 frames EU rules for third-country students and researchers. National law still runs local procedures. EUR-Lex hosts the authentic text.

text: A bachelor and master Stipendium call sets the intake calendar, eligible levels, and document checklist for applicants. Host universities confirm programme capacity under the call. Late uploads after the deadline are typically rejected by the system. Nominating partners publish country-specific notes. Applicants should export confirmation emails.
summary: The BA/MA Stipendium call fixes calendar, levels, and documents. Late uploads are usually rejected. Applicants should keep confirmation emails.

text: An international education webinar explained how citation-based assistants can paraphrase public immigration factsheets without replacing official advice. Speakers stressed allow-lists, robots.txt, and refusal when sources are missing. Students still must file on government portals themselves. Universities shared library guides for reading legal PDFs. The recording will be posted next week.
summary: A webinar covered citation-based assistants for public immigration factsheets. Speakers required allow-lists and refusal without sources. Students must still file on official portals.

text: Campus housing offices reported limited dormitory places for the autumn semester and pointed scholarship students to accommodation-allowance rules. Contracts should be read before declining a dorm offer. Private rentals need registration addresses matching permit files. Advisers warned about scams on social media groups. Waiting lists close when capacity is full.
summary: Dorm capacity is limited this autumn, so allowance rules matter. Address registration must match permit files. Students were warned about rental scams.

text: Language centres announced Hungarian preparatory programmes linked to scholarship pathways. Attendance rules and exam requirements are printed in programme handbooks. Students who fail language exams may lose progression into degree programmes. Fee-paying routes differ from scholarship seats. Centres advised early enrolment for September cohorts.
summary: Hungarian preparatory programmes have attendance and exam rules. Failed exams can block degree progression. Early enrolment was advised for September.

text: A regional client-service notice reminded residence-permit applicants to book biometrics slots within fifteen days after online submission for study extensions. Missed appointments can void cases. Students should bring passports and appointment codes. Peak weeks near semester start fill quickly. Email reminders are sent when slots open.
summary: Biometrics for study-permit extensions must be booked within fifteen days. Missed appointments can void cases. Peak weeks fill quickly.

text: Library workshops taught international students how to read university academic regulations and find credit, exam, and thesis rules. Staff demonstrated PDF search tips and bookmarking. Students compared English translations with Hungarian originals where both exist. Workshops run monthly during term. Slides are posted on the intranet.
summary: Workshops help students read academic regulations for credits, exams, and theses. English and Hungarian texts are compared when both exist. Sessions run monthly.

text: An Ombudsman-style advice clinic stressed that chatbot answers are not legal representation. Volunteers redirected visitors to OIF, Tempus, and university international offices for binding decisions. Printed checklists covered common document mistakes. The clinic logged anonymized question themes for training. No passport numbers were collected.
summary: An advice clinic said chatbots are not legal representation. Visitors were sent to OIF, Tempus, and university offices. Checklists covered common document mistakes.

text: Researchers comparing multilingual summarizers reported that mT5-small is a practical warm-up model before domain adaptation on education and immigration texts. They used tiny news slices for initial loss curves. Domain references still need human five-line summaries for ROUGE. Compute budgets on T4 GPUs limited full XL-Sum epochs. Results will feed a student portfolio project.
summary: mT5-small is used as a warm-up summarizer before domain adaptation. Tiny news slices support early loss curves. Human five-line references enable ROUGE checks.
